item.title: Mukta bodha intro
item.description: The most extensive surviving corpus of classical Śākta tantra belongs to the “crooked” goddess Kubjikā. Many of these texts were composed in the western Deccan, in what is now southern Maharashtra and Goa. Deeply indebted to the scriptures of the Trika, the worship of Kubjikā incorporates the “Ancient” tradition’s mantra system into its own distinctive visualization of the octagon-shaped Saṃvartāmaṇḍala, supplementing it with its own nyāsas and the iconic “pañcaprāṇava” mantras.
